summary_paragraph: A female patient with a history of paraplegia from a gunshot wound, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter use was admitted with bilateral flank pain, nausea, and vomiting. She had recently eloped from a prior admission for a complicated E. coli UTI after incomplete antibiotic treatment. This admission was complicated by active cocaine and alcohol use, with a brief episode of chest pain attributed to cocaine. Initial blood cultures showed gram-positive rods and cocci, but repeat cultures were negative, indicating contamination. She was treated with IV ceftriaxone, transitioned to oral Macrobid, and managed for musculoskeletal back pain with Neurontin and Ultram. She tolerated a regular diet, had no recurrence of symptoms, and was discharged home in stable condition with a full course of antibiotics and follow-up instructions.
